_comment: Pi's retry window, widened from its defaults (maxRetries 3, baseDelayMs
2000 => 2+4+8 = 14s). The proxy this swarm talks to goes away for ~60s at
a time — a Render instance OOMing and restarting — and 14s does not cover
that, so every record in flight died: a concurrency-32 run lost 96 of 100,
91 of them to Cloudflare 429 challenge pages in front of the restarting
instance. Observed failure durations clustered at 15.9s median, matching
the 14s backoff exactly.
6 retries at the same base gives 2+4+8+16+32+64 = 126s, comfortably past a
60s outage. Retrying inside Pi beats retrying the container: it resumes the
same session instead of re-spending the whole record's tokens.
Note retry.provider.maxRetries defaults to 0 — Pi disables the bundled
OpenAI SDK's own retries and does its own, so this block is the only knob.
Not fixed by anything server-side: these failures happen in front of the
litellm proxy, so litellm's num_retries never sees them.
This layer's backoff is plain `baseDelayMs * 2**(attempt-1)` — no jitter
and no knob for it, so N workers hitting one outage retry in lockstep.
The nested retry.provider.* layer (the bundled OpenAI SDK) does jitter and
does honor Retry-After, but it caps each sleep at 8s, so its +-25% spread
is a couple of seconds against a 60s outage — not enough to matter here,
and pi's docs warn it can swallow usage-limit errors before pi sees them.
Keep SWARM_CONCURRENCY moderate rather than relying on either.
